requirements.label: Science: EGCSE/SGCSE/IGCSE subject choices
requirements.details: For this school-certificate route, Mathematics or Additional Mathematics at C or better, plus Co-ordinated Sciences OR two of Additional Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Combined Science, Geography, ICT, Physics or Physical Science at C or better; another subject is also listed. The shared Additional Mathematics no-double-count rule applies. The row's six-credit wording and English D versus general English C must be read with the separate shared clarification; no grade waiver is inferred.

requirements.label: Science: GCE O-level science alternatives
requirements.details: The GCE O-level route names Mathematics/Additional Mathematics at C or better, then the pair Additional Combined Science and Combined Science OR two of Additional Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Geography, Physics or Science (Chemistry/Physics), plus any other subject. The source presents these as alternative science groups, not a requirement to take every listed science. Read the six-credit/English wording with the common clarification and do not double-count Additional Mathematics.

requirements.label: Science: COSC credit alternative
requirements.details: The COSC paragraph states at least five credits at C or better and the subjects listed in the preceding school-certificate subsection. It is an alternative qualification route, not a conversion into five IGCSE subjects or an established waiver of the university-wide English condition.

requirements.label: Science: possible Level 1 exemption after A-levels
requirements.details: At least two A-level grades of C or better in relevant science subjects offered at the university, or an equivalent qualification, may allow exemption from Level 1 if the applicant fits an acceptable major combination. The applicant may still have to take and pass first-year courses. This is possible advanced standing, not guaranteed admission directly to a later year or an IB/AP equivalence.

requirements.label: Electrical/Electronic Engineering: school-certificate subjects
requirements.details: The EGCSE/SGCSE/IGCSE paragraph lists six passes, with C or better in five subjects chosen to include Mathematics/Additional Mathematics; Co-ordinated Sciences OR Physics/Physical Science; one subject from Biology, Chemistry, Combined Science, Geography, ICT, Agricultural Technology, Food and Textile Technology, Business Accounting, Technical Studies or Design and Technology; and any other subject. The English D versus general C condition is separately flagged. The source's Co-ordinated Sciences and AND-group layout is retained; confirm its subject-count treatment rather than inventing an extra fixed combination.

requirements.label: Electrical/Electronic Engineering: GCE O-level alternatives
requirements.details: The GCE O-level paragraph lists six passes and five subjects at C or better, including Mathematics/Additional Mathematics; either Additional Combined Science with Combined Science, or Physics/Physical Science; one of Biology, Chemistry, Geography or ICT; and other subject(s). Do not require both alternative science groups. The shared English and total-credit clarification applies; no IB/AP conversion is supplied.

requirements.label: Electrical/Electronic Engineering: COSC alternative
requirements.details: COSC with at least five credits at C or better, including the subjects listed in the preceding EGCSE/SGCSE/IGCSE and GCE O-level subsections. The exact subject grouping and general-English interaction remain source-specific; this is not a promise of an automatic exemption.

requirements.label: Electrical/Electronic Engineering: A-level Mathematics and Physics
requirements.details: Acceptable A-level examinations or an equivalent qualification with grades of C or better in Mathematics and Physics may permit exemption from Level 1 of the BEng programme. Both named subjects are required for this stated advanced-standing option; exemption is discretionary, not guaranteed Year 2 placement.

requirements.details: Candidates from outside Eswatini must meet the published entrance requirements and obtain BOTH Admissions Committee and Faculty of Science and Engineering approval for admission to BEng Level 1. These are two required approvals, not alternatives or an additional language-score number.

requirements.label: Computer Science Education: school-certificate subject pool
requirements.details: For EGCSE/SGCSE/IGCSE: C or better in Mathematics/Additional Mathematics and two subjects from Accounts, Additional Mathematics, Agriculture, Biology, Business Studies, Chemistry, Combined Science, Design and Technology, Economics, Geography, Physics, Physical Science, Fashion and Fabrics, Food and Nutrition, Agricultural Technology, Food and Technology, Business Accounting, Technical Studies or ICT. Additional Mathematics cannot be reused if counted for the mathematics requirement. The shared English D/C clarification applies.

requirements.label: Computer Science Education: GCE O-level subject pool
requirements.details: For GCE O-level: C or better in Mathematics/Additional Mathematics and two from Biology, Additional Mathematics, Agriculture, Combined Science, Commerce, Chemistry, Economics, Geography, General Science, Human and Social Biology, Physics, Physical Science, Principle of Accounts (as printed), Fashion and Fabrics or Food and Nutrition. Recognized equivalents are mentioned on the continuation page. This specific GCE list does not include Home Economics or ICT, although those subjects appear in other technical programmes' lists; shared English and no-double-count rules apply.

requirements.details: For the Library Science option, the faculty paragraph lists C or better in at least four other subjects, alongside its English D wording. Read this with the common general-six-credit/English-C discrepancy rather than treating the option as an established four-subject-only offer. This option does not publish the separate Library Information Systems mathematics requirement.

requirements.label: Information Science: Library Information Systems option
requirements.details: For the Library Information Systems option, the paragraph specifies C or better in Mathematics/Additional Mathematics and at least four other subjects, alongside its English D wording. Mathematics belongs to this option; do not automatically impose it on the Library Science option. The university-wide six-credit/English interaction still needs confirmation.

requirements.label: Information Science: A-level entry and course exemption
requirements.details: Acceptable A-level examinations or an equivalent qualification may allow entry into Level 1 of either Library Science or Library Information Systems, with possible exemption from courses already passed at A-level. This is not stated as automatic Level 2 admission, nor as a numeric A-level or IB total.

requirements.label: Information Science mature route: aptitude paper
requirements.details: For the mature-age route, the special paper is an aptitude test under the Academic General Regulations. The existing shared mature-age conditions still apply. No numeric pass mark, test format, work-duration substitute or general test requirement for school-leavers is supplied.

requirements.label: Information Science diploma route restricted to Library Science
requirements.details: A recognized diploma in Information Science or equivalent qualification is admissible to the Library Science option. Senate determines the entry level and courses to take. The paragraph does not state the same diploma entitlement for the Library Information Systems option or a guaranteed advanced-entry year.

requirements.label: Geographic Information Science: diploma/associate-degree groups
requirements.details: The diploma subsection has two bullets: a relevant three-year Geography or related diploma (or equivalent); and a diploma or associate degree in GIS, Geoinformatics, Geomatics, GeoScience, Physics, Computer Science, Information Science, IT, Mathematics or Statistics, from a recognized institution. Each bullet assigns entry level/courses to Senate. It does not explicitly say whether both credentials are cumulative or identify an OR between the bullets; confirm the relevant route rather than requiring every listed diploma or guaranteeing placement.

requirements.label: Geographic Information Science: prior bachelor's-degree route
requirements.details: A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Science, IT, Physics, Mathematics, Statistics or a Geography-related degree from UNESWA or another recognized institution may support admission. requirements.label: Public Sector Accounting: Commerce-degree alternative
requirements.details: One OR-separated route is a Bachelor of Commerce degree or equivalent from UNESWA or another recognized university. It is not a requirement to also complete every professional or work-experience alternative. The programme is a postgraduate diploma, not a school-leaver undergraduate award.

requirements.label: Public Sector Accounting: completed professional qualification
requirements.details: Alternative route: a completed CA, ACCA, CPA, CIMA or another recognized professional qualification. Part-completed examinations are not declared equivalent to a completed qualification, and no universal five-year work rule is attached to this alternative.

requirements.label: Public Sector Accounting: non-Commerce wording and work field
requirements.details: Another OR-separated paragraph prints a non-Bachelor of Commerce from UNESWA or a recognized institution, AND experience in a Public Sector Accounting and Finance environment. The wording does not fully specify the award level intended by non-Bachelor of Commerce; confirm the qualification rather than assuming any unrelated certificate qualifies. Senate determines entry level and additional courses. No work-duration minimum is printed for this group.

requirements.label: Public Sector Accounting: AAT III plus five-year experience route
requirements.details: Alternative route: AAT Level III or equivalent AND five years of experience in a Public Sector Accounting and Finance environment. The qualification and work condition are cumulative within this option; five years is not extended to the separate BCom/professional alternatives. The 120 programme-completion credits printed below are graduation requirements, not prior-admission credits.

requirements.label: Law: BA Law holders and Year 3 course obligations
requirements.details: A BA Law degree holder is eligible for Year 3 of the conventional LLB programme, with no exemptions from courses in that year or subsequent years. This is not the same as promising exemptions for every completed bachelor's degree, and is not replaced by the distance-education subsection's placement wording.

requirements.label: Law: recognized law diploma and placement review
requirements.details: A Diploma in Law from UNESWA or an equivalent qualification from a recognized institution may support entry to LLB. Senate determines the entry level and courses to take. This is separate from the BA Law route's express Year 3 placement and supplies no automatic Year 3 entitlement for every diploma.

requirements.label: Science/Engineering: general C versus faculty D and credit counts
requirements.details: For the seven Science and Engineering degrees listed on page 31, general page 13 requires six C-or-better school passes including English C, while faculty pages 32–41 print English D in their school-leaver clauses. Some faculty rows call the set six credits despite English D, and Information Science gives option-specific other-subject counts. Both source statements remain; the prospectus does not clearly establish a general-rule waiver or precedence. Confirm exact English and total-credit applicability; the faculty D wording is not automatically a confirmed English-C exemption.

requirements.label: IT and Geographic Information Science: shared school-certificate pool
requirements.details: For EGCSE/SGCSE/IGCSE admission to Information Technology or Geographic Information Science: C or better in Mathematics/Additional Mathematics and two from Accounts, Additional Mathematics, Agriculture, Biology, Business Studies, Chemistry, Combined Science, Design and Technology, Economics, Geography, Physics, Physical Science, Food and Nutrition, Fashion and Fabrics, Home Economics, ICT, Agricultural Technology, Food and Textile Technology, Business Accounting or Technical Studies. These are choices, not twenty simultaneous subjects. The shared no-double-count and English clarification apply.

requirements.label: IT, GIS and Actuarial/Financial Mathematics: shared GCE pool
requirements.details: For GCE O-level admission to IT, Geographic Information Science or Actuarial/Financial Mathematics: C or better in Mathematics/Additional Mathematics and two from Biology, Additional Mathematics, Agriculture, Combined Science, Commerce, Chemistry, Economics, Geography, General Science, Human and Social Biology, Physics, Physical Science, Principle of Accounts (as printed), Food and Nutrition, Fashion and Fabrics, Home Economics or ICT. The pool is shared once for these three named programmes; the separate Computer Science Education pool is narrower. Read with the English and no-double-count clarifications.

requirements.label: Named science/technical courses: Additional Mathematics counted once
requirements.details: For the BSc science groups and Computer Science Education, IT, Geographic Information Science and Actuarial/Financial Mathematics subject lists, Additional Mathematics cannot count again as an optional subject if already used for the Mathematics/Additional Mathematics minimum. This is a counting restriction, not an extra compulsory third mathematics subject. Do not extend the footnote to unrelated programmes that do not print it.

requirements.label: Three Social Sciences degrees: six passes versus general six credits
requirements.details: The BA Social Science, BSW and LLB faculty paragraphs require six school passes, with English at C or better and at least four subjects at C or better. General page 13 instead says six passes all at C or better. The wording does not establish that five C grades plus a lower sixth pass is an approved exemption. Both statements are retained; confirm the overall credit count rather than deleting the sixth pass or silently replacing the general rule. This does not remove the separate Mathematics condition for named Social Science majors.

requirements.label: Four Consumer Sciences degrees: English, Mathematics and sciences
requirements.details: For BSc Food Science, Nutrition and Technology; BSc Consumer Science; BSc Consumer Science Education; and BSc Textile and Apparel Design and Management: SGCSE/IGCSE or an internationally recognized comparable certificate, with C or better in English Language, Mathematics and two science subjects. Science choices are Physics, Chemistry, Physical Science, Biology, Integrated Science and Combined Science. Read with the shared university-wide degree baseline; no different sixth-subject rule or IB/AP equivalence is invented.

requirements.label: Consumer Sciences: accepted home/food/textile science subjects
requirements.details: For the four named Consumer Sciences degrees, a credit at C or better in Home Economics, Home Management, Food and Nutrition, Fashion and Fabrics or Food and Textile Technology can be accepted as a science subject. These subjects are alternatives within the faculty science requirement, not five extra compulsory subjects and not a waiver of English/Mathematics.

requirements.label: Consumer Sciences: two- and three-year diploma placement
requirements.details: For the four named Consumer Sciences degrees, a relevant completed two-year Faculty of Agriculture UNESWA diploma (or equivalent) leads to Year 1; a relevant completed three-year diploma (or equivalent) leads to Level 3. These are OR-separated routes, not two diplomas required together. The relevant Home Economics versus Home Economics Education field conditions and course review still apply.

requirements.label: Consumer Sciences: diploma-course exemptions and missing earlier courses
requirements.details: Equivalent courses already taken in the relevant diploma may receive Senate-approved exemption on the Consumer Sciences Board's recommendation. Candidates must still take Level 1 or 2 courses not covered by their diploma. Level 3 admission therefore does not establish blanket exemption from every earlier-year course.

requirements.label: Other Consumer Sciences degrees: relevant Home Economics diploma
requirements.details: For the diploma-entry routes into Food Science, Nutrition and Technology; Consumer Science; and Textile and Apparel Design and Management, the relevant qualification named is a Diploma in Home Economics. The Home Economics Education diploma is specified separately for Consumer Science Education; the fields are not automatically interchangeable.

requirements.label: Consumer Sciences: A-level course exemption
requirements.details: For the Consumer Sciences degree group, courses already passed at A-level with C or better may be exempted. This concerns corresponding course exemptions, not a guaranteed full-year exemption, direct Level 3 admission or a new IB/AP score equivalence.
